CheckTitle: Ensure a dedicated security audit IAM role exists
Description: A dedicated IAM role with the SecurityAudit managed policy (or equivalent read-only access) should exist to enable security teams to perform audits of AWS resources without requiring elevated credentials. Absence of such a role forces security reviewers to use higher-privilege accounts.
Risk: Without a dedicated security audit role, security reviews require sharing credentials with broader permissions than necessary, violating least-privilege principles. This increases the risk of accidental or malicious modification during security reviews.
Remediation: Create an IAM role named SecurityAudit (or similar) and attach the AWS managed SecurityAudit policy (arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit). Configure a trust policy allowing assumption by the security team's identity provider or IAM principals.
SeverityBasis: AWS IAM documentation — Security best practices in IAM (grant least privilege for security operations roles); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AU-6 (Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting). Not a numbered control in CIS AWS 3.0.0; low severity reflects an operational gap rather than direct exploitation risk.
AuthoritativeSource: AWS IAM documentation — Security best practices in IAM; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — security audit role creation is not enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0
